366916.title: Conjecture on optimal logarithmic diameter and mixing bounds for bounded-rank groups
366916.statement:
Let $\underline{G}$ be a simply connected, simple algebraic group over $\mathbb{F}_{p}$, and let $\underline{x}=(x_{1},\ldots,x_{r})$ be a generating set of $\underline{G}(\mathbb{F}_{q})$. Define

$$
\mu:=\frac{1}{2r}\sum_{i=1}^{r}\left(\delta_{x_{i}}+\delta_{x_{i}^{-1}}\right).
$$

Let $\gamma$ denote the Cayley-graph diameter and $t_{\infty}(\mu)$ the associated mixing time. **The optimal logarithmic diameter and mixing conjecture.** In Corollary (1)+(2), the constant $O_{\underline{G}}(1)$ in the exponent of $\log$ can be taken to be equal to $1$:

$$
\gamma\leq O_{\underline{G}}(1)\log\left|\underline{G}(\mathbb{F}_{q})\right|,
$$

$$
t_{\infty}(\mu)\leq O_{r,\underline{G}}(1)\log\left|\underline{G}(\mathbb{F}_{q})\right|.
$$

This is presented as a stronger conjecture in the case of groups of bounded rank, improving the polylogarithmic bounds in the preceding corollary. The source gives no resolution status.

366916.ordinary_route_or_gap: Uniform logarithmic diameter AND mixing for all generating tuples. Polylogarithmic growth bounds do not improve their exponent to one by an algebraic rearrangement. No full expansion mechanism or in-scope counterexample developed.

367533.title: Aanderaa–Karp–Rosenberg conjecture for finite graph properties
367533.statement:
Let $V$ be a finite vertex set and let a **graph property** be a property of graphs on $V$ that is invariant under relabeling of the vertices. A graph property is **monotone** if adding edges preserves the property, and **nontrivial** if it is true for some graphs on $V$ and false for others. It is **elusive** if, in the Seeker–Hider edge-query game, Hider has a winning strategy forcing Seeker to query every pair of vertices before determining whether the graph has the property.

**Aanderaa–Karp–Rosenberg conjecture.** Every nontrivial monotone graph property is elusive.

The conjecture asserts that every nontrivial monotone graph property requires examining all possible vertex pairs in the worst case. It is a long-standing unresolved problem, originating in the 1970s; the paper discusses its failure for infinite vertex sets rather than resolving the classical finite version.

367533.ordinary_route_or_gap: Exact finite monotone evasiveness claim. A prime-power case or an infinite-graph failure does not resolve all finite vertex sets. No finite counterexample or general adversary established.

367967.title: Fritzsche–Külshammer–Reiche character-theoretic formula for the base size of ${\rm S}_{n,k}$
367967.statement:
Let $n\geq 2k$, let $G={\rm S}_{n,k}$, and let $H$ be a point stabiliser of $G$. Write $b(G)$ for the base size of the permutation group $G$, let $\mathcal{K}(G,H)$ be the Külshammer graph of $G$ with respect to $H$, let $\operatorname{Diam}(\mathcal{K}(G,H))$ denote its diameter, and let $1_H$ and $\operatorname{sgn}\!\downarrow_H$ denote respectively the trivial character of $H$ and the restriction to $H$ of the sign character. If $d(\alpha,\beta)$ denotes graph distance in $\mathcal{K}(G,H)$, then **Fritzsche–Külshammer–Reiche's conjecture.**

$$
b(G)=\operatorname{Diam}(\mathcal{K}(G,H))+1=d(1_H,\operatorname{sgn}\!\downarrow_H)+1.
$$

This conjecture proposes an alternative character-theoretic formula for the base size in terms of the Külshammer graph; the cited work of Fritzsche, Külshammer, and Reiche is presented as the source of the conjecture, and no resolution is given here.

368130.title: Hodge–Riemann conjecture for the intersection algebra of a line arrangement
368130.statement:
Let $V$ be an $n$-dimensional vector space, and let $E$ be a finite set of lines in $V^*$ that is not contained in a single hyperplane. Let $\mathsf{A}^*(E)=\bigoplus_{j=0}^n\mathsf{A}^j(E)$ be the graded algebra generated by the classes of polytopes whose facet conormals lie in lines of $E$, and let $\mathsf{K}(E)\subseteq\mathsf{A}^1_+(E)$ be the open cone defined by centrally symmetric polytopes having a facet conormal on every line of $E$. For a nonnegative integer $k\leq n/2$, choose $\ell_{C_0},\ldots,\ell_{C_{n-2k}}\in\mathsf{K}(E)$ and set

$$
\ell_{\mathbf C}=\ell_{C_1}\cdots\ell_{C_{n-2k}}.
$$

**Hodge–Riemann conjecture for $\mathsf{A}^*(E)$.** The map

$$
\mathsf{A}^k(E)\longrightarrow\mathsf{A}^{n-2k}(E),\qquad x\longmapsto x\cdot\ell_{\mathbf C},
$$

is injective. Moreover, if $x\in\mathsf{A}^k(E)$ satisfies $x\cdot\ell_{C_0}\cdot\ell_{\mathbf C}=0$, then

$$
\sigma(x)\cdot x\cdot\ell_{\mathbf C}\geq 0,
$$

with equality if and only if $x=0$. The conjecture is proposed as an analogue of the Hodge package for graded Möbius algebras and valuations, and would imply the Dowling–Wilson conjecture; the supplied text does not establish whether it has been resolved.

368270.title: Stable-part and stable-cover decomposition conjecture
368270.statement:
Let $\mathscr C$ be a dependent hereditary class of graphs. A **modelization** is the strong transduction pairing used in the paper. A **dependent hereditary class** is a hereditary class of graphs that is dependent, and a **stable hereditary class** is a hereditary class with no transduction containing all finite half-graphs. A partial order has a **stable cover graph** when its graph of covering pairs is stable.

**Stable-part decomposition conjecture.** Every dependent hereditary class of graphs has a modelization in a dependent hereditary class consisting of the expansion of a hereditary stable class of graphs by a partial order having a stable cover graph.

This is presented as the weakest non-trivial version of the proposed inverse decomposition conjecture, after observing that unrestricted posets would make such a statement vacuous. The supplied text gives no resolution.

368826.title: English–McCourt–Mattes–Phillips cocktail-party graph conjecture
368826.statement:
Let $G^c=(V,E)$ be a cocktail party graph, obtained from a complete graph on an even number of vertices by deleting a perfect matching. For a color $i\in[2]$, let $G^c_i$ be the spanning subgraph consisting of the edges of color $i$, and call a subset a diameter $2$ subset of $G^c_i$ when every two of its vertices have distance at most two in the induced subgraph.

**English–McCourt–Mattes–Phillips conjecture.** In every $2$-coloring of the edges of $G^c$, there exist $A,B\subseteq V$ and colors $i,j\in[2]$ such that

$$
A\cup B=V
$$

and $A$ and $B$ are diameter $2$ subsets of $G^c_i$ and $G^c_j$, respectively.

This conjecture asks for a two-set strengthening of the component-cover phenomenon in the first conjecture. The paper presents it as unresolved and studies related 2-reachable coverings.

368864.title: Mean-field weight-noise invariance conjecture
368864.statement:
Let the assumptions of Theorem~ hold, with the dynamics of $(\bm{X}_i(t))_{i\in[N]}$ and $(\bm{w}_{i,j}(t))_{i,j\in[N]}$ governed by the SDEs with weight-noise intensity $\eta>0$. Let $(\overline{X}(t),\overline{w}(t))$ solve the original McKean–Vlasov SDEs, without the $\eta$ term, with initial data from the same independent-mixture sampling. **Mean-field weight-noise invariance conjecture.** The estimates of the article still hold; in particular, for some constant $C(t)>0$ depending on $t$ and the bounds in Assumptions~ and,

$$
\mathbb{E}\bigg[\delta_{W_1,\square}\bigg(\Big((\bm{X}_{i}(t))_{i\in[N]},(\bm{w}_{i,j}(t))_{i,j\in[N]},[N]\Big),\Big(\overline{X}(t),\overline{w}(t),(\Omega\times\widehat{\Omega})\Big)\bigg)\bigg]\leq\frac{C(t)}{\sqrt{\log N}}.
$$

The conjecture asserts that independent edge noise has no effect on the limiting McKean–Vlasov dynamics under mean-field scaling, apart from the stated finite-size error.

369074.title: Conjectured joint equidistributions for pairs X^(4)_7 and Y^(4)_7

These are conjectured joint equidistributions of mesh patterns; the source provides no resolution, so their status remains open.

369088.title: Classification conjecture for equal determinants of colored paths
369088.statement:
Let $P$) and $Q$ be two colored paths on $m$ vertices with concentration matrices $K_P$ and $K_Q$ satisfying

$$
\det(K_P)=\det(K_Q).
$$

A **reflection** of a colored path is the path obtained by reversing its vertex order. **Colored-path determinant conjecture.** If $m$ is even, then one of the following holds: $Q$ is identical to $P$; $Q$ is a reflection of $P$; or $P$ and $Q$ satisfy the color configuration stated in the even-path theorem, or a reflection of that configuration. If $m$ is odd, then one of the following holds: $Q$ is identical to $P$; $Q$ is a reflection of $P$; or $P$ and $Q$ satisfy the color configuration stated in the odd-path theorem, or a reflection of that configuration. The claim is presented as an unresolved conjecture based on the necessary color-multiset conditions proved earlier.

370637.title: The periodic coloring conjecture
370637.statement:
Let $N\geqslant 1$, let $V$ be a finite set of primitive, nonzero, mutually incommensurable vectors in $\mathbb{Z}^2$, let $\Sigma$ be a finite color set, and let $\Omega\subset \Sigma^{|V|}\times (\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^2$. For each $v\in V$, choose a fixed primitive vector $\bar v$ orthogonal to $v$. Let $\operatorname{Coloring}(V,N,\Sigma,\Omega)$ be the set of tuples of functions $C_v\colon\mathbb{Z}\to\Sigma$ satisfying the local condition specified by the source, using a two-dimensional clock $\sigma\colon(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^2\to(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^2$.

**Periodic coloring conjecture.** For any $V$, $N$, $\Sigma$, and $\Omega$ as above, the solution set $\operatorname{Coloring}(V,N,\Sigma,\Omega)$ is not aperiodic.

This conjecture is presented as an equivalent reformulation of the periodic tiling conjecture in virtually-$\mathbb{Z}^2$ spaces. The source gives no resolution status.

371247.title: The totally sorted configuration and SYT probability conjecture for labeled chip-firing on star graphs
371247.statement: Let $\Delta^{k,m}$ be the star graph with $k$ branches, each receiving $m$ labeled chips, and consider the random labeled chip-firing process in which every firable vertex is equally likely to be selected at each stage and, after a vertex is selected, each chip there is equally likely to fire. A stable configuration is called **totally sorted** when chips $(1)$ through $(m)$ land on branch 1, chips $(m+1)$ through $(2m)$ land on branch 2, and so on, with chips $\left((k-1)m+1\right)$ through $(km)$ landing on branch $k$. **Totally sorted configuration and SYT probability conjecture.** The totally sorted configuration is the most likely stable configuration, and stable configurations corresponding to standard Young tableaux are more likely to occur than non-SYT configurations. This asks for a probabilistic refinement of the paper's structural results on reachable stable configurations: although reachable configurations can be mapped to row-increasing tableaux with increasing first and last columns, these conditions do not characterize all reachable configurations, and the conjectured probability comparison remains open.

371534.title: Li's contraction interlacing conjecture for matroid Chow polynomials
371534.statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a geometric lattice, let $a$ be an atom of $\mathcal{L}$, and let $\underline{\mathrm{H}}_{[a,\widehat{1}]}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{[a,\widehat{1}]}$ denote the augmented and ordinary Chow polynomials of the upper interval $[a,\widehat{1}]$, with $\underline{\mathrm{H}}_{\mathcal{L}}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{\mathcal{L}}$ the corresponding polynomials of $\mathcal{L}$. **Li's conjecture.** The augmented and ordinary Chow polynomials of the upper interval interlace those of $\mathcal{L}$:

$$
\underline{\mathrm{H}}_{[a,\widehat{1}]}\preceq\underline{\mathrm{H}}_{\mathcal{L}},\qquad \mathrm{H}_{[a,\widehat{1}]}\preceq\mathrm{H}_{\mathcal{L}}.
$$

Equivalently, for any simple matroid $\mathrm{M}$ on ground set $E$ and any $i\in E$, contraction satisfies $\underline{\mathrm{H}}_{\mathrm{M}/i}\preceq\underline{\mathrm{H}}_{\mathrm{M}}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{M}/i}\preceq\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{M}}$. The source describes this as a strengthening of the Chow-polynomial real-rootedness conjecture and gives no resolution.
371534.review_depth: literal statement plus selected actual primary text; see ORDINARY-ATTEMPTS.md and read-inventory.json
371534.ordinary_route_or_gap: Public arXiv:2610.17135v1 Corollary D disproves ordinary and augmented Chow real-rootedness. Interlacing in the literal real-rooted sense implies real-rootedness of both polynomials; choose a counterexample lattice and any atom to refute the universal conjunction. This is a routine public bridge, zero credit.

372029.title: The basis and generation conjecture for the Norton subalgebra of the bilinear forms graph
372029.statement:
Let $\Gamma=(X,\mathcal R)$ be the bilinear forms graph, let $x,y\in X$ be adjacent vertices, and let $U=U(x,y)$ be the subspace defined earlier. Let $E=E_1$ be the primitive idempotent, and let $\widehat O^{(B)}_{1,1}$, $\widehat O^{(C)}_{1,1}$, and $\widehat O^{(D)}_{1,1}$ denote the indicated vectors associated with the corresponding cells of the equitable partition. The Norton product on $EV$ is $u\star v=E(u\circ v)$. **Basis and generation conjecture.** The following hold: 

(i) The subspace $EU$ has basis

$$
E\hat x,\qquad E\hat y,\qquad E\widehat O^{(B)}_{1,1},\qquad E\widehat O^{(C)}_{1,1},\qquad E\widehat O^{(D)}_{1,1}.
$$

(ii) The Norton subalgebra $EU$ is generated by $E\hat x$ and $E\hat y$. 

This conjecture concerns the structure of the Norton algebra associated with the $Q$-polynomial bilinear forms graph. Establishing the proposed basis and generation statement would give an explicit description of the Norton subalgebra determined by two adjacent vertices.

382408.title: Basis conjecture for the alternating component of generalized diagonal coinvariants
382408.statement:
Let $m,n$ be positive integers, let $L_{mn,n}^+$ denote the set of rational $m$-Dyck paths, and let $L_{n,n}^+$ denote the set of Dyck paths of size $n$. For any rational Dyck path $\pi\in L_{mn,n}^+$ and any $i\in\{0,1,\dots,m-1\}$, let $\pi^i\in L_{n,n}^+$ be the Dyck path defined by the decomposition in the source, and let $\Delta_{\zeta^{-1}(\pi^i)}$ denote the associated alternating generalized diagonal coinvariant. **Basis conjecture.** The collection

$$
\left\{\prod_{i=0}^{m-1}\Delta_{\zeta^{-1}(\pi^i)}\right\}
$$

over all $m$-Dyck paths forms a basis of the alternating component of the space of generalized diagonal coinvariants. This conjecture proposes a combinatorial basis indexed by the decomposition of rational Dyck paths; its resolution depends on identifying the stated products with a basis of the alternating generalized diagonal coinvariant component.

362579.title: Higashitani–Kummer–Michałek conjecture for complete multipartite graphs
362579.statement:
Let $K_{a_1,\dots,a_k}$ be a complete multipartite graph, and let $E_{a_1,\dots,a_k}$ denote the Ehrhart polynomial of its symmetric edge polytope. Let

$$
\operatorname{CL}=\{z\in\operatorname{\mathbb{C}}\colon\Re(z)=-\frac{1}{2}\}
$$

be the canonical line. Two real-rooted polynomials **interlace** when their roots alternate on a common totally ordered set.

**Higashitani–Kummer–Michałek conjecture.** (i) For any complete multipartite graph $K_{a_1,\dots,a_k}$, the roots of $E_{a_1,\dots,a_k}$ lie on $\operatorname{CL}$. (ii) If $a_1\leq\dots\leq a_k$, then $E_{a_1,\dots,a_k}$ and $E_{a_1,a_2,\dots,a_k-1}$ interlace on $\operatorname{CL}$.

This extends the known result for symmetric edge polytopes of $K_{1,n}$, $K_{2,n}$, and $K_{3,n}$, and would give a broad class of $\operatorname{CL}$-polytopes. The conjecture remains open in the general complete multipartite case.

362722.title: Caterpillar symbic tree basis conjecture
362722.statement: Let $E$ be the ground set of matrix entries, and let $\mathcal{B}\subset E$ be a set of size $2n-1$. A **symbic tree** is a combinatorial object indexing a maximal cone in the tropical variety of rank-two symmetric matrices; a **caterpillar symbic tree** is a symbic tree whose branches are caterpillars, meaning that each branch contains only one cherry. **Caterpillar symbic tree basis conjecture.** The set $\mathcal{B}$ is a basis of the matroid of some symbic tree if and only if $\mathcal{B}$ is a basis of the matroid of some caterpillar symbic tree. This would reduce the determination of all bases in the relevant matroid to symbic trees with caterpillar branches; the preceding proposition establishes the analogous statement for the union of bases of the algebraic matroids, but the conjectured equivalence for each basis is not resolved here.

362958.title: Endpoint invariance conjecture for s-Cambrian congruences
362958.statement:
Fix an $n$-tuple ${\boldsymbol{s}}$ of non-negative integers and an ${\boldsymbol{s}}$-arc $\alpha$. Let $\equiv_\alpha$ be the $\alpha$-Cambrian congruence of the ${\boldsymbol{s}}$-weak order, and let $W_{\boldsymbol{s}}/\equiv_\alpha$ be its $\alpha$-Cambrian lattice. Let the canonical join complex be the simplicial complex formed by canonical join representations of elements of this lattice, and let the ${\boldsymbol{s}}$-Cambrian foam and quotientoplex be the associated quotient polyhedral structures.

**Endpoint invariance conjecture for s-Cambrian congruences.** For fixed ${\boldsymbol{s}}$, the following depend only on the endpoints of $\alpha$: the cardinality of the $\alpha$-Cambrian lattice; the $f$-vector of its canonical join complex; the isomorphism class of its undirected cover graph; and the isomorphism class of the face lattice of the $\alpha$-Cambrian foam, equivalently of the $\alpha$-Cambrian quotientoplex.

This predicts that several combinatorial and polyhedral invariants are insensitive to the interior data of the arc. The source presents it as the main conjecture on ${\boldsymbol{s}}$-Cambrian congruences and gives no resolution.

362958.ordinary_route_or_gap: Conjecture 75 explicitly contains four invariants. Global reversal may exchange all interior sides, but does not give arbitrary same-endpoint arc transformations. Need local flip bijections preserving canonical joins and polyhedral incidences; none established.

362959.title: Orientation invariance conjecture for s-permutree lattices
362959.statement:
Fix an $n$-tuple ${\boldsymbol{s}}$ of non-negative integers and a decoration map ${\boldsymbol{\delta}}$ assigning one of the four local orientations—none, up, down, or up-down—to each index $i$ with $s_i\ne0$. Let $W_{\boldsymbol{s}}/\equiv_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}$ be the ${\boldsymbol{\delta}}$-permutree lattice, and let its canonical join complex be the simplicial complex formed by canonical join representations.

**Orientation invariance conjecture for s-permutree lattices.** For fixed ${\boldsymbol{s}}$, changing any up decoration to a down decoration in ${\boldsymbol{\delta}}$ does not affect the cardinality of the ${\boldsymbol{\delta}}$-permutree lattice or the $f$-vector of its canonical join complex.

The conjecture concerns invariants that remain unchanged under the indicated decoration change, while the source notes that other structures, such as the undirected cover graph and face lattices, can depend on the positions of the up and down decorations. No resolution is supplied.

363751.title: The conjectured bases for distinguished subspaces of the fundamental module
363751.statement:
Consider the $Q$-polynomial distance-regular graph $\Gamma=(X,\mathcal R)$ of diameter $D$, its standard module $V$, and the fundamental $\mathbb T$-submodule $\Lambda\subseteq V^{\otimes 3}$. Let $E_r^{*(k)}$ and $E_r^{(k)}$ denote the dual and ordinary primitive-idempotent operators acting on the $k$th tensor factor, and let $P_{a,b,c}$ and $Q_{a,b,c}$ be the vectors defined in the paper. **The conjectured bases for distinguished subspaces of the fundamental module.** The following sets are conjectured to be bases of the indicated subspaces:

$$
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
\text{Subspace}&E_0^{*(1)}\Lambda&E_0^{*(2)}\Lambda&E_0^{*(3)}\Lambda\\
\hline
\text{Conjectured basis}&\{P_{0,i,i}\}_{i=0}^D&\{P_{i,0,i}\}_{i=0}^D&\{P_{i,i,0}\}_{i=0}^D
\end{array}
$$

$$
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
\text{Subspace}&E_0^{(1)}\Lambda&E_0^{(2)}\Lambda&E_0^{(3)}\Lambda\\
\hline
\text{Conjectured basis}&\{Q_{0,i,i}\}_{i=0}^D&\{Q_{i,0,i}\}_{i=0}^D&\{Q_{i,i,0}\}_{i=0}^D
\end{array}
$$

These conjectured bases would give explicit descriptions of six natural subspaces associated with the three tensor factors and the ordinary or dual idempotents. Their verification is posed as a direction for future research.
